lessons.chapterTitle: How to Work a Support Ticket

slots.practicalActivity: Using Meridian Steel Fabricators' Ticket #40112 (invoice INV-88341 won't validate) as your scenario, work the full six-stage ticket workflow yourself: write the intake note, assign a severity, state the two isolating questions (one record or many? one user or everyone?), and list exactly where in Oracle Fusion you'd look to confirm a theory (the Holds tab, a job log, an interface table, or a diagnostic report) before touching anything. Finish by writing both a "bad" one-line resolution note and a "good" five-part resolution note for the same ticket so the difference is concrete.
slots.deliverable: A ticket-workflow worksheet with an intake note, isolating questions, a named evidence source, and both a bad and a good resolution note for the same ticket.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for How to Work a Support Ticket: build a personal one-page ticket-triage checklist combining the six workflow stages, the four isolating questions (one record or many, one user or everyone, did it ever work, what changed recently), and the five-part resolution-note template. Test it by writing three one-line ticket descriptions of your own (for example, "invoice won't validate," "user can't see a business unit," "bank statement won't reconcile") and running each through the checklist to confirm it produces a sensible first investigation step.
slots.deliverable: A reusable one-page ticket-triage checklist plus three worked test-run examples showing it in use.

lessons.title: Ticket: AP Invoice Will Not Validate

slots.practicalActivity: Work Cascade Outdoor Supply's Ticket #40189 (invoice INV-55032 held on Price): compare the PO price ($42.00) to the invoiced price ($46.50) and decide, with justification, which of the three possible fixes — correct the PO, correct the invoice, or manually release the hold — is actually right given the supplier's mid-quarter price increase. Then independently re-solve Meridian's INV-88341 distribution-mismatch ticket from the earlier lesson before checking your answer against the guide.
slots.deliverable: Two complete resolution notes, each naming the specific root cause and the chosen fix with a stated justification.

slots.practicalActivity: Work Harbor & Vance Logistics' Qty Rec hold ticket (500 units ordered, 500 invoiced, only 320 received) and decide which of the PO, receipt, or invoice is actually the wrong document. Then work BrightPath Facilities Group's Potential Duplicate Invoice ticket by comparing the two source PDFs line by line to confirm it is a true duplicate rather than two legitimate same-amount invoices, and write the cancel/void action you would take.
slots.deliverable: Two resolution notes, each identifying which specific document was wrong and the exact action taken to correct it.

lessons.title: Ticket: Payment Is Missing from GL

slots.practicalActivity: Work all three remaining Payables tickets: find why a payment already Accounted – Final still hasn't transferred to GL, diagnose a Failed Document Validation PPR down to the one supplier (Keystone Rigging Supply) missing a bank account, and resolve Cascade Outdoor Supply's Alpine Trail Gear payment-terms ticket by correcting both the supplier-site setup AND the 6 already-entered invoices still carrying the wrong Net 30 terms.
slots.deliverable: Three resolution notes, with the payment-terms note explicitly separating the setup fix from the fix to already-affected data.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Payables Tickets: simulate a one-day AP support queue. Given five one-line ticket descriptions you write yourself, one for each hold type covered in this chapter (Price, Qty Rec, Potential Duplicate, Failed Document Validation, and a payment-terms default), triage each by assigning a severity and naming which Oracle Fusion screen you would open first (the Holds tab, the Resolve Payment Validation Errors page, or the supplier site) — the goal is fast, correct routing, not full resolution yet.
slots.deliverable: A triage log for five simulated AP tickets, each with an assigned severity and a named first screen to check.

lessons.title: Ticket: AR Does Not Reconcile with GL
Ticket: Receipt Applied to the Wrong Invoice

slots.practicalActivity: Work Harbor & Vance Logistics' $9,000 AR-to-GL reconciliation gap: isolate it to a manual journal posted directly to the AR control account, then decide to reverse that journal and re-enter the same adjustment as a proper Receivables transaction instead of leaving it in GL. Then work BrightPath's misapplied-receipt ticket by tracing the $4,100 receipt to the correct invoice (INV-9042, not INV-9039) and listing every downstream place a misapplied receipt could still show up (customer statements, dunning notices, credit limit).
slots.deliverable: Two resolution notes, one reversing-and-re-entering a direct GL journal and one unapplying-and-reapplying a receipt with a downstream-impact checklist.

lessons.title: Ticket: Bank Statement Will Not Reconcile

slots.practicalActivity: Work Meridian Steel Fabricators' 18-transaction AutoInvoice rejection by tracing all 18 lines in `RA_INTERFACE_ERRORS_ALL` to one missing tax rate code. Then resolve Cascade Outdoor Supply's "missing invoice on statement" complaint by proving it's a cutoff-date timing issue, not a data error. Finally, sort Thornfield Materials Holdings' 14-line bank reconciliation exception queue into its three real categories (normal bank fees, normal outstanding checks, and the two genuine errors) and fix only the two that are actually wrong.
slots.deliverable: Three resolution notes, with the reconciliation-queue note explicitly separating the 12 normal exceptions from the 2 genuine data errors it corrects.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Receivables and Cash Tickets: write a one-page "working as designed vs. genuinely broken" reference guide. List at least four real examples from this course where the system was working correctly and the real fix was explanation rather than correction (the statement cutoff-date exclusion, normal outstanding checks, normal bank fees, and an intentional setup choice you've seen elsewhere in this course) versus four examples where it was a genuine data or setup error needing a fix.
slots.deliverable: A one-page reference guide with four "working as designed" examples and four "genuinely broken" examples, each drawn from a real ticket worked so far.

slots.practicalActivity: Work Thornfield Materials Holdings' journal-won't-post ticket by diagnosing the specific block in the posting process. Then work Harbor & Vance Logistics' Journal Import failure: trace all 60 EF04 "invalid account" rows to a new payroll cost-center segment value, confirm dynamic insertion is off for this ledger, and decide to create the account combination properly through Enterprise Structures rather than simply switching dynamic insertion on.
slots.deliverable: Two resolution notes, with the Journal Import note explaining specifically why dynamic insertion should stay off for this ledger.

lessons.title: Ticket: Accounting Failed in Subledger Accounting
Ticket: Subledger Entries Did Not Transfer to GL
Ticket: Accounting Period Will Not Close

slots.practicalActivity: Work Cascade Outdoor Supply's intracompany-balancing SLA failure using the Accounting Event Diagnostic report logic, and write the missing intracompany balancing rule it needs. Work BrightPath's "Accounted – Final but never in GL" ticket by distinguishing an intentional Transfer to GL = N setting from a timing gap. Then work Thornfield's October period-close ticket by reading its Close Monitor checklist and resolving both blockers (the disabled-account journal and the untransferred Payables batch) using the specific method each one actually matches, instead of "just try closing again."
slots.deliverable: Three resolution notes, with the period-close note explicitly citing which earlier ticket pattern each of its two blockers matched.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for General Ledger and Subledger Tickets: build a one-page GL/Subledger failure decision tree, using the real field and report names from this chapter, that routes a new ticket to the right fix based on its specific symptom — a journal that exists but won't post, rows that never reached GL (Journal Import/EF04), accounting itself failing (an SLA balancing rule), accounted-but-not-transferred (a timing gap vs. an intentional Transfer to GL = N), and a period that won't close (the Close Monitor checklist tying all of the above together).
slots.deliverable: A one-page GL/Subledger failure decision tree a new support analyst could follow using real Oracle Fusion terminology.

lessons.title: Ticket: Asset Depreciation Did Not Run
Ticket: Mass Additions Are Not Posting

slots.practicalActivity: Work Meridian Steel Fabricators' stamping-press depreciation ticket: confirm it's isolated to one asset rather than the whole book, trace it to an On Hold Mass Additions line missing an asset category, and fix the in-service date so depreciation catches up for the month it missed. Then work Cascade Outdoor Supply's six-truck Mass Additions batch failure by tracing all six lines to one missing depreciation-expense-account setup on the new vehicle category and reprocessing all six in a single pass.
slots.deliverable: Two resolution notes, with the six-truck note explaining why one category-setup fix clears all six lines at once.

lessons.title: Ticket: Expense Report Is Stuck in Approval
Ticket: User Cannot Access a Business Unit

slots.practicalActivity: Work Harbor & Vance Logistics' stuck-expense-report ticket by tracing it to a blank HR manager field rather than anything in Expenses itself. Work BrightPath's new-AP-clerk business-unit access ticket by distinguishing job-role/function-privilege access from data-role/security-profile access. Then work Thornfield's "can't see the other division's journals" question by confirming, across multiple controllers, that a segment value security rule is an intentional restriction rather than a bug, and write a note that explains it instead of "fixing" it.
slots.deliverable: Three resolution notes, with the segment-value-security note explicitly justified by the cross-controller consistency check that ruled out a misconfiguration.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Assets, Expenses and Setup Tickets: write a one-page "function access vs. data access vs. segment value security" reference card using the real tickets just worked. State in your own words what each layer controls and which specific symptom (page won't open, page opens but search returns nothing, page and search work but one division's data is missing) points to which layer.
slots.deliverable: A one-page security-layer reference card distinguishing function privilege, data role/security profile, and segment value security by symptom.

slots.practicalActivity: Work Meridian Steel Fabricators' FBDI load failure by tracing it to a deleted template column rather than bad data in any of the 300 rows. Then work Cascade Outdoor Supply's ADFdi version-mismatch ticket by tracing the workbook integrity error to a weekend environment patch rather than a data problem. Write both resolution notes so each explicitly states whether the cause was file/version hygiene or data content, and why that distinction changed the fix.
slots.deliverable: Two resolution notes, each explicitly naming the cause as file/version hygiene versus data content.

lessons.title: Ticket: REST API Call Returns an Error
Ticket: Report Shows the Wrong Numbers

slots.practicalActivity: Work Harbor & Vance Logistics' REST API 400-error ticket: confirm it's a content error rather than a 401 credentials error, trace it to a quarterly Oracle update that made `BusinessUnit` a required field, and use the resource's describe metadata to confirm nothing else was missed. Then work LTV Manufacturing Corporation's "Balance Sheet doesn't match Smart View" ticket by getting the exact dollar gap, checking the as-of timing of each report, and proving the $340,000 difference is a timing difference, not a data error.
slots.deliverable: Two resolution notes, one written for a developer audience (the REST integration fix) and one for a finance audience (the timing-difference explanation).

slots.practicalActivity: Course capstone review: build a consolidated support methodology field guide covering every module in this course — Payables, Receivables and Cash, General Ledger and Subledger, Assets/Expenses/Security, and Data and Integration. For each module, list the real symptom-to-cause patterns worked across the course (a distribution mismatch, a stale PO price, a Qty Rec receiving gap, a direct-journal AR break, an EF04 invalid account, an intentional Transfer to GL = N setting, segment value security, a deleted FBDI template column, a REST required-field change, and a report timing difference), so the result is a working reference you could actually keep open while triaging real Oracle Fusion Financials tickets.
slots.deliverable: A multi-section support methodology field guide covering every ticket pattern from the course, organized by module.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can work a real Oracle Fusion Financials support ticket end to end: isolate whether a problem is one record or many, trace it to its actual root cause using the right evidence (a holds tab, a job log, an interface table, or a diagnostic report), apply the narrowest correct fix across Payables, Receivables, Cash Management, GL, Subledger Accounting, Fixed Assets, Expenses, security, and data integration, and document the resolution to audit standard.
